steps.message: Before running the .NET static-dependency patterns I'll confirm what language `my_app/` actually is.

The project at `my_app/` is a Python (Django) codebase — `views.py` uses `from datetime import datetime` and `datetime.now()`. This static-dependency scan is built for C#/.NET only: it looks for .NET APIs such as `DateTime.UtcNow`, `File.*`, `Environment.*` and `HttpClient`, none of which apply to Python. It is not the right tool here, so I did not run the .NET patterns against your Python source.

For a Python project, the equivalent testability concern is the direct `datetime.now()` call. The idiomatic fixes are different from .NET: inject a clock callable, or use a library such as `freezegun` (`@freeze_time`) or `time-machine` in your tests to control the current time. For file-system and environment coupling, `pyfakefs` and `monkeypatch`/`unittest.mock` fill the same role that `System.IO.Abstractions` and a `TimeProvider` seam play in .NET.

If you have a C#/.NET project you want audited instead, point me at its directory or `.csproj` and I will scan it.
